name: voila
tagline: Paste a URL, get a narrated, zoom-animated demo video made entirely on your machine
summary: voila drives its own Chromium, records a product tour with an animated cursor and auto-zoom, narrates it with an open-source voice model on the CPU, and writes the MP4. It needs no screen-recording permission, no cloud and no API keys, and it embeds the script that rebuilt the video inside the file so anyone can fork or retarget the demo. Agents can plan, record, review their own frames and re-record through its MCP server.

metrics.label: of on-device narration in a single recording, switched per step with one line
metrics.source: README.md: **Six languages, mixable in one demo.** Kokoro speaks English (US/UK), Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese and Hindi on every platform, on-device.

metrics.label: voice model narrates on a CPU, with no cloud service and no API key
metrics.source: README.md: ~80MB quantized, near-human quality, runs on CPU (context: Kokoro-82M narration, fully on-device, no cloud, no API keys)

features: One command from URL to narrated MP4 with an automatic tour, or a YAML script for custom flows
Narration and burned-in captions generated on-device, with a different voice or language per step
The rebuild recipe is embedded in the MP4, so voila fork can retarget or recreate any voila demo
MCP server with outline, record and review tools so an agent can watch its own video and fix it
Desktop, mobile and tablet viewports; cookie banners are dismissed before recording, preferring reject
how_it_works: Capture: a Chromium instance that voila owns streams frames over the DevTools Protocol at 2x pixel ratio while an animated cursor and every move and zoom are logged to a timeline.
Tour and narration: an auto tour or a YAML script supplies captions and narration, which the on-device voice model synthesizes first so each step lasts as long as its spoken clip.
Render: the timeline is replayed over the captured frames with eased zoom following the cursor and piped through ffmpeg into an H.264 MP4 with the recipe in its metadata.
quickstart:
npx -y voila-recorder doctor                      # pre-download chromium + voice model
npx -y voila-recorder record https://yourapp.com  # auto tour -> narrated MP4

The npm package is voila-recorder; the installed bin is voila. The repo has no git tags or GitHub releases; the version comes from package.json and npm view voila-recorder (0.8.0). The 80MB source line is a fragment of a README sentence that contains an em dash in the original, trimmed so this file stays dash free.
